title: Finite supported-diagonal normalization equality
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the normalized Chern and diagonal data of [def-sp-tower-class-diagonal]. Use finite underlying-abelian-sheaf forgetting, exact evaluation, the root map $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ and boundary comparison of [def-sp-tower-class-finite]. The ordinary direct image along the actual diagonal is exact. Define its supported finite integer quotient by the unique residue-multiple-of-one formula on constant generators over every pulled-back chart of [def-sp-tower-class-pullback]. Evaluate the supported diagonal arrow using the exact single and shift comparisons and the normalized finite Tate-line realization. Finite diagonal normalization is the equality saying that this arrow, after forgetting scalars and precomposing with the supported integer quotient, is the evaluated signed Cartier boundary followed by the positive Kummer connecting morphism and the root map. All sources, targets, shifts and quotient maps are fixed.

proof.text: At each level, identify the actual constant-ring direct image with the conjugate of fixed-scalar lowerStar through sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence, using uniqueness of right adjoints and openSquarePullbackModel. The diagonal is closed and locally of finite presentation since the projective line is smooth over its base. Apply finite direct-image exactness. Evaluation is jointly faithful, as morphisms of system sheaves are determined on each pair (level, chart). The exact conservative-family criterion and ordinaryPushEvaluation therefore give both finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation of the system direct image.

Push forward the integral finite quotient of the projective line and postcompose with the inverse of the underlying-abelian-sheaf ordinaryPushEvaluation comparison. The comparison cancels its inverse, and the defining formula of finiteQuotient gives the required value on each pulled-back constant generator.

The ambient constant integer sheaf maps epimorphically to diagonalIntegralSource by the integral generation lemma. Cancel that epimorphism. Sheafification uniqueness reduces equality to constant presheaf generators. Apply the injective component of the ordinaryPushEvaluation isomorphism; both maps then equal the same residue multiple of one. This proves uniqueness and fixes the supported quotient without changing any endpoint or normalization definition.

Form the degree-zero single quotient and the shifted root map using the generic singleBoundaryEquality helper. Reuse evaluatedDiagonal for the evaluated coefficient arrow and then forget scalars. Unfolding the helper, evaluatedDiagonal and forgetEvaluatedArrow gives the original finiteBoundaryEquality expression; local let bindings share the four arguments. No object, transport, sign or equation changes.
